parameters.content:
## Track certificate and insurance expiry dates in Google Sheets and send escalating email reminders

### How it works

1. A schedule trigger fires at 7am daily and reads the whole compliance register from Google Sheets.
2. A Code node compares every Expires date to today and sorts rows into expired, within-7-days, within-30-days and within-90-days buckets.
3. An IF gate ends the run silently on days when nothing is due, so the workflow never nags.
4. A second IF splits anything already expired away from merely upcoming renewals.
5. Expired items trigger an urgent "you may not be covered" email; upcoming ones get a calmer renewals summary, with the 90-day horizon list included only on Mondays.

### Setup steps

- [ ] Connect Google Sheets credentials and point "Get expiry register from Google Sheets" at your compliance sheet.
- [ ] Give the sheet the columns Item, Type, Holder, Expires, RenewalContact, Notes and enter every policy, certificate and registration once.
- [ ] Add SMTP credentials and replace owner@example.com in both email nodes.
- [ ] Adjust the 7am cron in "Run daily expiry check at 7am" to match your working day.

### Customization

Change the 7/30/90-day thresholds in "Sort items into expiry windows" to match your own renewal lead times, or add a Slack or SMS node next to "Send expired items alert email" for louder escalation.

---

Built by [Digital Dots](https://digitaldotsent.com)

## 1. Read the register daily

The **Run daily expiry check at 7am** schedule trigger fires every morning, then **Get expiry register from Google Sheets** pulls every certificate, policy and registration row - each with its expiry date - into the workflow.

## 2. Bucket by days remaining

The **Sort items into expiry windows** Code node compares each expiry date against today and groups every item into one of four buckets: already expired, within 7 days, within 30 days, or within 90 days.

## 3. Decide whether to email

**Continue only if something needs action** stays silent when nothing is due, so you get no empty emails. **Check for already expired items** then splits genuinely expired items away from the ones merely approaching their deadline.

## 4. Send the escalating alert

**Send expired items alert email** raises an urgent cover-lapse warning; **Send upcoming renewals email** sends a calmer heads-up for what is coming due. Two tones, so an expired certificate never reads like a routine reminder.
